label: Bhakti-Pratikūla-Bhāva Varjanāṅgīkāra Song Four
title: āmi to’ swānanda-sukhada-bāsī
metaDescription: Bhakti-Pratikūla-Bhāva Varjanāṅgīkāra Song Four (viṣaya-vimūḍha ār māyāvādī jan) of Śaraṇāgati (‘Surrender’) written by Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura in 1893. This songbook contains 50 songs detailing the six symptoms of surrender unto the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

verses.translation: Oh I am a resident of Svānanda-sukhada-kuñja, and a maidservant of the lotus feet of Rādhikā and Mādhava.
I happily rejoice at the union of the Divine Couple, and in Their separation I die in utter anguish.
I never look at the area in Vraja called Sakhī-sthalī where Candrāvalī and her friends live. If I were to see that place it reminds me of Candrāvalī’s sharp-tongued gopī friend named Śaibyā.
I feel pain in my heart whenever I happen to catch sight of Candrāvalī’s proud girlfriends, for they are all inimical to Rādhā’s camp.
Candrāvalī wants to take away Rādhā’s Lord Hari, thus causing the love-grove of Rādhikā to be overcast with the darkness of gloom.
I never look at the faces of those who wish to obstruct the joy of the union of Śrī Rādhā and Govinda.
Nor do I find any pleasure in conversing with those who are members of a camp opposed to Rādhā.
Bhaktivinoda has entrusted his soul with great care unto the lotus feet of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.Sixth Principle of Surrender: Bhakti-Anukūla-Mātra Kāryera
